name: Foum El Bouir
hero_subtitle: Atlantic wave spot on the ocean side of the peninsula — surf and open-sea energy beyond the lagoon.

overview.title: Ocean side of Dakhla
overview.p1: While the lagoon is flat and protected, Foum El Bouir faces the open Atlantic with real swell. It is the go-to wave zone for surfers, bodyboarders, and advanced kiters seeking authentic ocean conditions.
overview.p2: Access is straightforward by road along the peninsula from town. Always check wind, tide, and local swell conditions — the open ocean requires more experience than the calm lagoon shallows.
overview.p3: Not a beginner flat-water classroom, but an incredible spot for wave riding and dramatic sunset views over the Atlantic horizon.

q1.question: Is Foum El Bouir free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes, the beach and surf spot are entirely open and free to access at any time.

q2.question: What is the best time to go to Foum El Bouir?
q2.answer: It depends on the ocean swell and tide forecasts, but late morning to afternoon is popular for surfers and watching the waves.

q3.question: Is Foum El Bouir good for beginners?
q3.answer: Foum El Bouir faces the open Atlantic with real swell and waves, making it better suited for intermediate to advanced surfers and kiters rather than absolute beginners.

q4.question: How long should I spend at Foum El Bouir?
q4.answer: Plan around 2 to 3 hours for a surf session, beach walk, or relaxing at a nearby café overlooking the ocean.

q5.question: Can I rent gear or eat nearby?
q5.answer: Yes, surf schools and beach spots operate right along the area to rent equipment and serve refreshments.
